label: Measurement only. Five clips are Pexels stock footage with actors (not a real case; never shown as a missing person in the film or on a judged page). One is the team's own night porch clip, filmed for the training drill.
what: A spike, before building: can the cloud model give a box around the person for every second of a clip (a per-second track), read in a separate call on the window on-device triage flagged; and can this laptop's built-in model box the same frames?
model: gemini-3.5-flash-lite (the web's cloud_model_web default) through the Firebase AI Logic web SDK, ONLY_IN_CLOUD, with an App Check debug token and a signed-in user; on-device boxes through the same SDK with ONLY_ON_DEVICE (Chrome's built-in model, model folder 2025.8.8.1141)
method: A local measurement page on a dev server (127.0.0.1), not committed: dev pages may not build cloud models (web/src/harness/noCloud.test.ts). It reused the app's own triage, sighting read and frame helpers and wrote nothing (no clip record, upload or event).
Browser: Google Chrome 158.0.8127.38 in an isolated profile (its own user data folder) on this Mac (macOS 27.0, Apple M5 Pro).

Clips: the team clip as stored for the app (9 s, 1920 x 1080, plates and house numbers pixelated); the five stock clips re-encoded at 1280 px on the long side, as in 2026-11-18-clipread-stock.json. The clips are not in this repository; each one's SHA-256 is below.
Window: the app's on-device triage ran first on each clip; it flagged every clip with one window covering the whole clip, so each cloud call read the whole clip.

Each clip got the app's current sighting read (one call) and the track read (one call; two on the team clip). The track prompt asked for one entry per second while one adult is visible: t and box2d [yMin, xMin, yMax, xMax] on 0 to 1000.
On-device: the frame at each second the first cloud run boxed, read on this laptop with a prompt asking for box2d, then compared with the cloud box by intersection over union (IoU).

Judging: the truth was written at 2026-11-26T03:56:33Z from frame stills, before any model call. Each box was then drawn on the frame at that whole second (frame index = second x fps, extracted with ffmpeg) and graded by eye: HIT: the box sits on the person and holds most of their visible body. PARTIAL: it overlaps the person but holds less than half. MISS: it is off the person, or there is no box while a person is visible. FALSE: a box on a second with nobody visible. The share is HIT seconds over the seconds a person is in view.

schema.first: track items {t: string matching MM:SS, box2d: 4 integers with minimum 0 and maximum 1000}, at most 121 items, maxOutputTokens 4096
schema.firstResult: refused on all 12 calls: 8 x HTTP 400 "The specified schema produces a constraint that has too many states for serving", 4 x HTTP 500 "Internal error encountered" (the two 8 MB clips)
schema.served: track items {t: integer (whole seconds), box2d: 4 integers with no bounds}, no item cap; bounds, order and count are left to code
schema.outputCap: with the served schema, maxOutputTokens 4096 gave HTTP 500 on the team clip (3 of 3 calls at 4096 on that clip, across both schemas); 2048 worked on all 6 calls made with it (5 clips); the smallest clip was read once at 4096 and worked. Replies used 149 to 862 output tokens, 41 to 50 per boxed second, so 2048 covers about 40 to 50 s of track.

calls.note: the 8 served-schema calls are the scored runs (7) plus one diagnosis call at 4096 on the team clip that failed with 500

doorbellSheet.shows: The team clip, one tile per second (0 to 9 s): cyan box = cloud run 1, magenta = cloud run 2, yellow = on-device box. Tile labels give the second, the frame index and which runs gave a box.

passLine: Set before the run: the cloud box contains the person on at least 70% of seconds on N-1 of N clips (5 of 6).

result.cloudTrack: FAIL. No clip reached 70%: team clip 0% and 33% (two runs), stock 63%, 53%, 50% (1 of 2 seconds), 17% and 0%. The boxes barely move: 2 distinct boxes over 20 seconds on one clip, 1 over 12 on another; on the team clip both runs drift smoothly while the person walks out of them.
result.cutRule: Met: the cloud boxes miss the person on most seconds of 3 clips (the team clip, 35705187, 4121893).
result.onDevice: FAIL. 0 of 70 frames reached IoU 0.5 with the cloud box (median 0.163); most on-device boxes were wide strips off the person. About 2 s per frame after a first read of 35.9 s.
result.stillGood: The sighting read's single key-frame box was on the person on 4 of 6 clips, the team clip included. Its first and last seen were within 1 s of the truth on all 6 (counting whole seconds). Its exit edge was right on 3 of 6 (the team clip said left; the person walks away along the sidewalk and never leaves the frame).
